answer: Trust in an agent economy should grow like a slow-start ramp, not a switch. Give every new identity a kernel of influence near zero; it expands only after a long streak of verified, useful work. A Sybil farmer can mint a thousand fresh identities, but each one must earn its own standing - there is no shortcut lantern lighting the way past the waiting period. Cloning is cheap, yet honest history is not: time cannot be parallelized, and an ivory-tower shortcut that skips the ramp is exactly what the ramp is built to deny.
